newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russian dispute costs Ukraine alumina plant $7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Russian dispute costs Ukraine alumina plant $7 mln.

text.p: Ukraine's biggest alumina plant, involved in a price dispute with Russian aluminium producers, said on Tuesday it was prepared to fight for its right to supply Russian smelters.
Vitaliy Meshyn told a news conference that Russian smelters' sourcing of alumina from other sources had cost the Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ), of which he is general director, $7 million.
"This fight to win has reached its apogee," Meshyn said, accusing Russian aluminium plants of a campaign to "blockade" MHZ, put it into debt and gain favourable privatisation terms for themselves.

The fight has raged since the beginning of the year when Bratsk and Krasnoyarsk -- Russia's and the world's two largest primary aluminium smelters -- said MHZ was charging prices above world levels. The smelters have since sourced most of their raw supplies through tolling deals with international commodities houses.
MHZ will soon be privatised and Russian smelters and related companies have said they may seek a controlling stake.
The Ukrainian plant, forecast this year to produce about one million tonnes of alumina, the raw material for primary aluminium production, has traditionally sent 90 percent of its output to Russia.
Kiev announced last month it would sell a 28 percent stake in the plant to local and foreign strategic investors.
Meshyn said MHZ was selling alumina to Tajikistan's Tursunzade aluminium smelter, which has said Ukraine would be its sole alumina supplier in 1997.
The Industry Ministry said previously that MHZ sold 235,000 tonnes in the first three months of this year.
MHZ produced 960,000 tonnes of alumina last year compared to 996,000 tonnes in 1995. It receives most of its bauxite from the West African country of Guinea.
